guides.title: Keep your loadout in a predictable order
guides.description: Send weapon categories to familiar slots so switching takes less thought.
guides.edition: Battle Royale / Zero Build · Preferred Item Slots
guides.scope: Battle Royale / Zero Build · Preferred Item Slots
guides.quick: Assign categories in Settings → Game → Preferred Item Slots.
steps: Open Settings and select the Game tab.
Find Preferred Item Slots and choose Configure.
Assign your commonly used weapon categories to the slots you prefer.
Leave a slot for healing or other consumables, then apply the changes.
In a match, keep an inventory slot empty and pick up a matching item.
Check its position before practising the corresponding weapon-switch control.
guides.needs: Access to Game settings and a supported Battle Royale playlist.
guides.success: A matching pickup goes to the intended slot.
troubleshooting: Inventory full? The documented routing requires at least one empty slot.
Consumables moving right? Review Auto-Sort Consumables to Right as well.
guides.trouble: Inventory full? The documented routing requires at least one empty slot. Consumables moving right? Review Auto-Sort Consumables to Right as well.
guides.note: This is category routing, not a saved list of particular guns. Check your installed client if menus differ.

guides.title: Review one mistake in a match replay
guides.description: Use a recent match to notice missed cover or a late rotation.
guides.edition: Battle Royale · PC / PlayStation / Xbox replay support
guides.scope: Battle Royale · PC / PlayStation / Xbox replay support
guides.quick: Open Career → Replays and choose a recent recording.
steps: In Settings → Game, check that the appropriate replay recording option is enabled.
Play a match, then return to the lobby.
Open Career and choose Replays.
Select the recent match and press Play.
Review the moment before elimination; look for cover and the safe-zone route.
Write one change to try in your next match. Rename a replay if you want to keep it.
guides.needs: A supported platform and a match recorded by the current game version.
guides.success: The replay plays and you identify one practical adjustment.
troubleshooting: No recording? Enable recording before the next match; it cannot recreate an unrecorded match.
Old file will not open? Replays depend on the game version; saving does not guarantee compatibility.
guides.trouble: No recording? Enable recording before the next match; it cannot recreate an unrecorded match. Old file will not open? Replays depend on the game version; saving does not guarantee compatibility.

guides.title: Reduce avoidable connection delay
guides.description: Check your connection before changing your aiming settings.
guides.quick: Pause heavy network traffic and compare the same playlist under similar conditions.
steps: Stop large downloads, uploads and streams on the connection.
Use a wired connection if your device supports it.
Open Settings → Game → Language and Region.
Review Subregion Preference if this option is available in your region.
Try the same playlist again and compare responsiveness.
Keep the change only if it helps; expect a possible matchmaking wait trade-off.
guides.needs: An online match and access to the device network and Game settings.
guides.success: You can tell whether connection changes improve the delay.
troubleshooting: Still delayed? Internet routing or server congestion can remain outside your control.
Longer queue after a preference change? Reconsider that preference; it can affect matchmaking.
guides.trouble: Still delayed? Internet routing or server congestion can remain outside your control. Longer queue after a preference change? Reconsider that preference; it can affect matchmaking.

guides.title: Survive Ambush returning through the rooms
guides.description: Treat each pass as part of an encounter that may continue.
guides.edition: DOORS · The Hotel · ordinary run without modifiers
guides.scope: DOORS · The Hotel · ordinary run without modifiers
guides.quick: Hide for the approaching pass, listen as it moves away, and be ready to hide again.
steps: Recognize the approaching rushing sound and find a usable hiding place.
Enter as Ambush approaches your room.
Listen until it moves away before leaving the hiding place.
Stay beside that hiding place instead of opening more rooms.
Hide again when the returning sound approaches.
Repeat as needed; continue only after the encounter has ended.
guides.needs: An Ambush encounter, audible cues and a usable hiding place.
guides.success: You survive its passes and can continue through the Hotel.
troubleshooting: Hit on the return? Stay ready after the first pass; Ambush can rebound.
Timing feels different? Use sound, not a fixed bounce count or countdown.
guides.trouble: Hit on the return? Stay ready after the first pass; Ambush can rebound. Timing feels different? Use sound, not a fixed bounce count or countdown.
guides.note: Modifiers and other floors are outside this guide. Indexed wiki text was checked; no live run was tested.

guides.title: Pass Eyes without staring at it
guides.description: Keep the glowing entity out of view while crossing the room.
guides.edition: DOORS · The Hotel · ordinary run without modifiers
guides.scope: DOORS · The Hotel · ordinary run without modifiers
guides.quick: Turn the camera away from Eyes and move to the next door.
steps: Notice the blue-purple glow when entering a room.
Turn your camera away from the cluster of eyes immediately.
Keep the camera low or toward a clear wall while checking your route.
Move around obstacles without turning the camera toward Eyes.
Open the next door and continue once Eyes is gone.
guides.needs: Working camera controls and an Eyes encounter in the Hotel.
guides.success: You reach the next room without taking further damage from looking at Eyes.
troubleshooting: Health still falling? Check where the camera points, not only where your character moves.
Lost the doorway? Turn gradually while keeping the glowing area out of view.
guides.trouble: Health still falling? Check where the camera points, not only where your character moves. Lost the doorway? Turn gradually while keeping the glowing area out of view.
guides.note: This response is specific to Eyes. Other entities, including Screech, have different counters.

guides.title: Choose the real door when Dupe appears
guides.description: Track the room number before labels become scrambled.
guides.edition: DOORS · The Hotel · ordinary run without modifiers
guides.scope: DOORS · The Hotel · ordinary run without modifiers
guides.quick: Remember the last door number and choose the next number in sequence.
steps: Read the number each time you pass through a numbered door.
When several exits appear, stop before approaching a lock.
Work out the next number from the door you just used.
Choose the matching exit; do not test a suspicious lock.
Listen cautiously for the rumble from a false door if uncertain.
Update your remembered number after entering the next room.
guides.needs: A regular Hotel run with door labels visible at entry.
guides.success: You progress through the correct exit without a Dupe attack.
troubleshooting: Labels scrambled? The key label can scramble too; it is not a guaranteed backup.
No rumbling? Modifiers can remove that cue; this guide excludes those runs.
guides.trouble: Labels scrambled? The key label can scramble too; it is not a guaranteed backup. No rumbling? Modifiers can remove that cue; this guide excludes those runs.
guides.note: No fixed door offset or guessing trick is assumed.

guides.title: Move a knocked teammate out of danger

steps: Check your Limited Interact binding in Settings.
Identify nearby cover and check for enemies before approaching.
Stop sprinting beside the knocked teammate.
Use Limited Interact to pick them up.
Move to the chosen clear space and use the same binding to put them down.
Reassess the area before beginning the normal revive interaction.

troubleshooting: Carry does not start? Stop sprinting and check the custom binding.

guides.scope: Brawl Stars · current Gadget cooldown system

Enter a suitable practice or match mode.

collections.label: DOORS Hotel starter reference
collections.note: 12 selected threats and supplies for ordinary Hotel runs on PC and mobile. Not a complete DOORS encyclopedia. Modifiers and other floors can change these rules. Community article text was checked through the search index; direct Fandom access was blocked.

entries.name: Ambush
entries.summary: A rushing threat that can return after passing.
body: Stay close to a hiding place between passes.

entries.name: Eyes
entries.summary: A glowing cluster that hurts players who look at it.
body: Different entities require different responses.

entries.name: Dupe
entries.summary: False numbered doors punish careless entry.
body: Track the sequence as you enter each room.

entries.name: Figure
entries.summary: A major Hotel threat encountered in the Library and Electrical Room.
facts: Temporary stun, not a full banish
body: Watch its route and keep space. Crouching is not permission to walk into Figure or remain directly in its path.

entries.name: Halt
entries.summary: An encounter that asks you to change direction as it blocks the route.
body: Follow the encounter cues instead of relying on a fixed room number or an old guaranteed-spawn claim.

entries.name: Timothy
entries.summary: A small spider jumps from a looted container and briefly startles the player.
body: Timothy is a looting hazard, not a hallway chase. Recover your view and continue checking the room for other threats.

entries.name: Room Key
entries.summary: A key belongs to a specific locked door.
body: Search accessible areas before spending another tool. A scrambled label during Dupe is not a reliable shortcut to the correct exit.

entries.name: Lockpick
entries.summary: A consumable tool can bypass many ordinary locks.
body: It is useful when finding a normal room key would take time. Check the type of lock before expecting it to work.

entries.name: Flashlight
entries.summary: A directional light that needs battery charge.
body: Save charge for dark sections. An empty flashlight needs batteries rather than repeated attempts to switch it on.

entries.name: Lighter
entries.summary: A small fuel-based light for nearby surroundings.
body: Turn it off when light is unnecessary. Lighting it can make sound, so consider nearby threats before using it.

entries.name: Vitamins
entries.summary: A consumable gives a temporary movement-speed boost.
body: Use the speed for a planned route. It does not replace learning a chase path or watching obstacles.

entries.name: Crucifix
entries.summary: A held defensive item can restrain eligible entities.
facts: Seek and Figure only briefly stunned
body: Keep moving during a boss stun. A temporary restraint is not a completed chase or permission to stand beside the boss.

collections.label: PUBG PC starter reference
collections.note: 12 selected weapon families and maps from the publisher directory. This is not a full weapon-stat database or a current map-rotation list. Individual ammo, attachments, balance and availability should be checked in-game.

entries.name: Assault rifles (AR)
entries.summary: A flexible weapon family suited to many middle-distance fights.
body: Use the official family list to identify a weapon, then inspect the actual gun and compatible ammunition in the current game. Family membership alone does not make every rifle handle the same.

entries.name: Designated marksman rifles (DMR)
entries.summary: A family intended for controlled attacks at middle and longer distances.
body: This category helps separate a range-focused weapon from a close-range option when planning a loadout. Compare the actual item rather than assuming all DMRs share ammunition.

entries.name: Submachine guns (SMG)
entries.summary: A family associated with mobility and quick fire in close fights.
body: Recognize the category when deciding what role a pickup fills. Close-range usefulness does not make it the right choice for every distant target.

entries.name: Sniper rifles (SR)
entries.summary: A range-focused family built around accurate, powerful shots.
body: Use the family as a starting point for comparison. Read the weapon and ammunition information rather than expecting identical firing behaviour across the whole category.

entries.name: Shotguns
entries.summary: A family suited to sudden close encounters.
body: Learn the particular shotgun before rushing a doorway. The official directory groups several designs here; their reload and firing behaviour need individual practice.

entries.name: Handguns
entries.summary: Compact secondary firearms provide another equipment option.
body: Check the equipped item rather than assuming every handgun fires the same way. The directory includes both pistol and revolver designs.

entries.name: Melee weapons
entries.summary: Hand-held weapons are used at contact distance.
body: The short reach is the key difference from firearms. Do not approach a distant opponent expecting the same options as a ranged weapon.

entries.name: Throwables
entries.summary: Thrown utility offers different ways to pressure opponents or create cover.
body: Read the item name before using it. The throwable category includes tools with very different purposes; a smoke and a frag are not interchangeable.

entries.name: Special weapons
entries.summary: The official ETC directory groups equipment beyond the main firearm families.
body: This is a mixed directory, not one shared firing style. Read each item’s controls and availability before building a plan around it.

entries.name: Erangel
entries.summary: An island combining open grassland, mountains and built-up settlements.
body: Compare open ground with nearby buildings before choosing a route. This is a map introduction, not a promise that Erangel is in every current queue.

entries.name: Miramar
entries.summary: A desert battleground with exposed terrain and long sightlines.
body: Consider where cover ends before crossing barren ground. The official overview highlights its suitability for snipers; that does not prescribe one mandatory loadout.

entries.name: Taego
entries.summary: A large map with varied terrain and landmarks including Ho San Prison.
body: Use the live match map to plan a route between the current circle and nearby terrain. Queue availability and special mechanics are separate from this basic map reference.

collections.label: Wuthering Waves starter reference
collections.note: 12 selected attributes, weapon families and progression terms. This is not a complete character roster, build ranking or item database. Community article text was checked through the search index; no in-game combat test was performed.

entries.name: Glacio
entries.summary: An attribute associated with cooling and freezing.
body: An attribute labels damage and related effects. Read the specific skill instead of assuming every Glacio attack automatically applies a status.

entries.name: Fusion
entries.summary: An attribute associated with heat and ignition.
body: Weapon family and attribute are separate labels. Read a skill’s actual effect before choosing gear for it.

entries.name: Electro
entries.summary: An attribute associated with electrical charge.
body: Only attacks with the relevant effect apply Electro Flare; the attribute label alone is not a full skill description.

entries.name: Aero
entries.summary: An attribute associated with airflow.
body: Aero Erosion is a status associated with certain attacks and effects. Check the skill text rather than expecting every Aero hit to apply it.

entries.name: Spectro
entries.summary: An attribute associated with light and photons.
body: Spectro Frazzle is a stacking effect used by particular abilities. Do not infer an entire rotation from the attribute icon.

entries.name: Havoc
entries.summary: An attribute associated with annihilation.
body: Havoc Bane is a particular status effect, not a guarantee attached to every Havoc attack. Read the ability or encounter rule that applies it.

entries.name: Sword
entries.summary: One equipment family with several different secondary-stat options.
body: Choose between actual effects and stat needs. The shared Sword label does not make these items equivalent.

entries.name: Broadblade
entries.summary: A weapon family used by Resonators such as Jiyan and Taoqi.
body: The same family includes different secondary stats. Compare the character’s needs before investing in one.

entries.name: Pistols
entries.summary: A weapon category with damage-focused and utility-focused options.
body: Compare the item effect as well as its stat.

entries.name: Gauntlets
entries.summary: A weapon category whose items can support different stat needs.
body: Match the item to the Resonator’s actual scaling.

entries.name: Rectifier
entries.summary: An equipment family containing both damage and support-oriented stat options.
body: A shared family does not imply the same role. Compare the weapon’s full effect before equipping it.

entries.name: Data Bank
entries.summary: The Terminal system records Echo discoveries and affects Echo collection progression.
body: Check your own Data Bank screen for current level requirements. Repeating an already-recorded rarity is different from discovering a new entry; old level-cap tables may no longer apply.

research.purpose: Curated beginner expansion; not a complete encyclopedia or live patch validation.
limitations: No guide was playtested. sourceChecked records a reading date, not proof the method worked in a live match.
DOORS and Wuthering Waves community pages were read through indexed article text because direct Fandom requests returned 402/robots restrictions. Indexed content can lag current updates.
Historical official patch notes establish documented mechanics and interface paths, not the latest installed behaviour. Versions are identified per guide.
Advice such as reviewing one mistake, preserving a preset, and choosing cover is an original practical exercise grounded in the documented feature.
No API response, game screenshot, peer feedback, gameplay success or exhaustive coverage was fabricated.
